Bio: I build software for both sides of the counter: the businesses that run on it and the people who use it every day. Over the past year I've also rebuilt how that software gets built, starting with how I work myself.I came into technology from the operator side. I managed a club, owned a women's fitness center and spa, and spent almost a decade selling software to operators. In 2012 I co-founded Club Apps to give health clubs their own branded mobile apps, and we sold it to Netpulse. I still lead like a founder: know the customer's P&L, ship what moves it, and don't confuse activity with progress.Today I'm SVP of Product at ABC Fitness. I lead product across Ignite, Glofox, and Trainerize, the platforms behind gyms, studios, and coaches around the world, along with FitMetrics, an AI-assisted coaching platform we acquired this year. The work runs from pricing and partnerships to member apps used by millions of people.On AI, I went first. I rebuilt my own work around agents for research, analysis, drafting, and decision prep before I asked anyone else to change. Then we brought it to the whole product org: a leadership workshop, an all-hands, AI tools for every product manager, and AI-built intelligence briefs. The tools I built for my team are now used across product, and I've taught the same approach to sales and marketing. We ship noticeably faster than we did a year ago.In the product, we launched ABC's first AI-powered capabilities, starting with the AI Workout Builder, which puts AI inside the coach's workflow and keeps the coach in charge. I'm also working on one of the more interesting questions in software right now: how to price AI by the action instead of the seat.What I've learned is that the tools are the easy part. The real work is redesigning workflows, being clear about who owns what, holding the quality bar, and helping people build new habits without feeling replaced.Mobile is where all of this lands for customers. I've spent my career connecting B2B systems with consumer experiences, from Club Apps to ABC's member engagement app to HYROX training inside the apps operators already use. I think AI will change that connection more than anything since the smartphone: software that understands intent and acts on it, with people still in control.I serve on the board of the Fitness Industry Technology Council, mentor women across our organization, and always enjoy comparing notes with leaders working through the same shift.

Bio:
How do you move a global, technology-driven supply chain closer to customers who are spread out across three continents — and what does that even look like? As the person responsible for the supply chain in various industries, it's my job to answer these questions and demonstrate the value of our approach to our customers, investors, and employees.

I start by focusing on the customer experience because the reality of the 21st century supply chain is that it starts and ends with each customer's digital experience. It begins when they purchase the product (typically online) and ends when it arrives at their door, as the result of a complex process that is completely transparent to them.

It's my job to deliver products to customers by building a supply chain that's both operationally efficient and agile enough to respond to the challenges that are certain to arise.

My experience as a Naval officer responsible for mission-critical logistics in the U.S. Navy Submarine Force, as well as my current reserve role as Commander NAVY Expeditionary Logistics Support Group, has served me well in the civilian workforce managing international supply chains for major companies like GE Capital, Stanley Black & Decker, Sensata Technologies and iRobot.

My primary focus is always on streamlining a companies global supply chain to move it closer to customers, reduce costs, increase sustainability and resilience, and accelerate the design, engineering, and prototyping of our products. Ultimately, I look to build the most seamless, flattened, and forward-leaning consumer product supply chain in the world.
